# make-localllm-easier

> One command (`localllm`) that picks, downloads and runs the most accurate local LLM for a PC's GPU and the user's language, chosen from measured benchmark scores, with llama.cpp tuned for AMD, NVIDIA, Intel and Apple GPUs. MIT license. Python CLI on PyPI: `pip install make-localllm-easier`.

## Use
- `localllm`: detect GPU/RAM, pick model, download llama.cpp + model, start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, open chat page
- `localllm doctor`: which model sizes (4B-120B MoE) fit this GPU, at which quantization, estimated speed, context capacity
- `localllm chat`: chat in the terminal with streaming and history
- `localllm eval --langs en,ja`: multiple-choice accuracy of any OpenAI-compatible server (Global-MMLU-Lite 23 languages, INCLUDE 44 countries, ThaiExam)

## Key measured facts (RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Windows, llama.cpp Vulkan)
- Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2 GB): English 81.8%, ~50 tok/s with MTP drafting
- gemma-4-26B-A4B QAT Q4 (13.3 GB): English 82.2%, ~69 tok/s
- 2-bit quantization costs 8-13 points; Hindi, Arabic, Thai lose most (13)
- Language-specific imatrix calibration gives no gain at ~3.5 bits
- AMD/Intel without Resizable BAR: set GGML_VK_DISABLE_HOST_VISIBLE_VIDMEM=1 for up to 1.7x decode (llama.cpp#27097)
